children: Soybean futures traded above $13.1 per bushel, near their highest level in almost three years supported by stronger Chinese demand for US supplies and expectations of further purchases ahead of high-level US-China talks.

China has already passed the halfway mark of its commitment to purchase 25 million metric tons of US soybeans, while recent US export sales have remained firm, confirmed at about 1.7 million metric tons, driven largely by Chinese demand.

The buying comes ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping next week, raising hopes for progress on agricultural trade and potentially lower tariffs on US farm goods.
Meanwhile attention remains on the US harvest, with heavy Midwest rains slowing fieldwork in some areas and potentially providing near-term support to prices.
Brazil’s 2026/27 crop is also in focus as planting gets underway, with forecasts pointing to another record harvest, although growth is expected to be modest.

title: Soybeans Remain Firm Ahead of Trump-Xi Talks
